scenario.name: AWS CIRT & Unit 42 DFIR — AWS CloudTrail IMDSv1 Role Theft, Off-Instance Replay & S3 Data Events Forensics
scenario.overview: Imagine a sunlit city park with green lawns, shade trees, winding stone footpaths, wooden benches, and a tiered stone water fountain at the center. Strolling along the city park footpath like an ordinary afternoon walker, a covert courier sits on a wooden bench near the stone fountain and tapes a coded note underneath the armrest. In this real-world scenario, the intruder quietly copies a trusted access pass from the park ranger's station, then smuggles copied records out past the park gate footpath in tiny disguised batches. A watchful park ranger at the corner kiosk notices the exact same bench receiving repeated timed drop-offs and logs the suspicious pattern on the patrol board. In this scenario (T1552.005, AWS CIRT & Unit 42 DFIR, AWS CloudTrail IMDSv1 Role Theft, Off-Instance Replay & S3 Data Events Forensics), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: eC2 Instance Metadata Service SSRF Query, then off-Instance STS GetCallerIdentity Replay, then s3 Data Event GetObject Burst. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering EC2 Instance Metadata Service SSRF Query, then Off-Instance STS GetCallerIdentity Replay, then S3 Data Event GetObject Burst, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection pivots on CloudTrail Event 200 correlated across the documented kill chain.

stages.title: Stage 1: EC2 Instance Metadata Service (IMDSv1) SSRF Query & STS Token Retrieval
stages.subtitle: Credential Access (T1552.005 - Unsecured Credentials: Cloud Instance Metadata API)
stages.description: Strolling along the city park footpath like an ordinary afternoon walker, a covert courier sits on a wooden bench near the stone fountain and tapes a coded note underneath the armrest. Specifically in Step 1, the intruder quietly copies a trusted access pass from the park ranger's station while everyday visitors and the park ranger go about their routine. The attacker sends an HTTP request to a vulnerable web proxy on EC2 instance i-0a1b2c3d4e5f60001 pointing to http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/ProdAppInstanceRole. Because IMDSv1 does not require a PUT session token with a TTL hop limit of 1, the metadata endpoint returns the temporary AccessKeyId (ASIA...), SecretAccessKey, and Token (logged in Network Event 200 with MetadataEndpoint=169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/, IamRoleName=ProdAppInstanceRole, IssuedAccessKeyPrefix=ASIA... , Temporary STS Credential, ImdsVersion=IMDSv1 , No X-aws-ec2-metadata-token header so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes HTTP SSRF Target: http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/ProdAppInstanceRole (which Queries the link-local Instance Metadata Service endpoint , http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/<RoleName> to retrieve so that harvests cloud identity tokens, escalates IAM privileges, or exfiltrates cloud data , T1552.005 during "EC2 Instance Metadata Service , IMDSv1 SSRF Query & STS Token Retrieval" without deploying traditional endpoint malware, captured in CloudTrail / Unified Audit Log telemetry).
